conflicts.fact: Distance covered by Group C compared with the straight-line walker, and what Group C's final location is
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says Group C walked the zigzag (about 30 m) then retraced to a midpoint, with a 'similar total distance', and ended in a different location. Lesson 2 says Group C had 'the same distance as the straight-line walker' (20 m) but a smaller displacement. The Lesson 1 data (20 m straight vs 30 m zigzag) means distances are not the same, so the puzzle is framed inconsistently.

conflicts.fact: Whether a negative acceleration/velocity indicates a change of direction or only slowing down
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says negative acceleration means slowing down, and a boda-boda slowing has negative acceleration while still moving forward. It also says the retracing walker 'experienced acceleration' due to a change in direction of velocity. Lesson 7 says 'a negative value indicates a change in direction or slowing down'. Lesson 4 says the sign encodes direction while also saying negative means slowing down.

conflicts.fact: Which graph's slope gives velocity vs acceleration, and which lesson covered d–t graphs
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8's model-building says to draw a connector arrow from the 'earlier d–t graph model (Lesson 7)', but d–t graphs were taught in Lessons 5 and 6; Lesson 7 covers v–t graphs. Lesson 7 itself refers to Lessons 5 and 6 as the d–t lessons.

conflicts.fact: Speed unit and values used in boda-boda examples
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 boda-boda brakes from 80 km/h to 20 km/h in 3 s (u=22.2, v=5.6 m/s, a=−5.53 m/s², Ngong Road). Lesson 8 boda-boda in Kisumu goes 0 to 30 km/h in 10 s, runs 20 s, then stops in 5 s. These are different boda-boda scenarios, but Lesson 8 says it needs ~21 m to stop from 30 km/h: area of a triangle is 0.5 × 8.33 m/s × 5 s ≈ 20.8 m, which is consistent. No conflict beyond context.

Lesson 7 uses a 42-minute 'training run' of Kipchoge with velocities up to 5.8 m/s and calls the table 'marathon splits'. The anchoring phenomenon and Lessons 5, 6 and 10 treat a 42 km marathon. Lesson 4 gives Kipchoge a run of 500 m east then 200 m west. The velocity of 5.6 to 5.2 m/s over the last 12 minutes ('42 minutes' as a run time versus 42 km distance) is inconsistently framed.

Lesson 4 says a mango falls 7.2 m from rest and reaches the ground at 12 m/s. From v²=2gs with g≈9.8, v≈11.9 m/s, so it is consistent, but Lesson 4's learned content says acceleration formula a=(v−u)/t only; no conflict on facts.

Lesson 2 has a matatu 30 km from Thika to Nairobi and back to Thika. Lesson 4 has a matatu braking on Thika Road accelerating 20 to 35 m/s northward; Lesson 4's overview also lists a boda-boda overtaking on Nakuru highway. These are different examples, not conflicting.

conflicts.fact: Where learners kept their first prediction
conflicts.versions: Lesson 10 says learners re-read their first prediction in 'science journals'. Lesson 1 had learners write predictions in exercise books.

conflicts.fact: Zero average velocity vs displacement for Kipchoge
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says Kipchoge's 42 km displacement is far smaller than distance run; Lesson 6 says his graph ends near zero gradient; Lesson 10 says displacement is nearly zero. The Lesson 4 problem gives him 500 m east then 200 m west (300 m displacement), whereas the anchoring phenomenon says a few hundred metres from the start.
